text:
Nina: FYI - noticed a burst of pending tiny-gang pods in ap-southeast1 during the morning compact run, looks like warm-pool slots stayed pinned on a set of nodes and we couldn't reclaim them.
Diego: I saw that too, plus a cluster-level increase in preemptive evictions for non-gpu workloads around 08:22 local.
Harpreet: Logs show warmpool.guard=true on a subset of nodes and the scheduler skipped preempt because netheal reported transient packet drops to the management plane.
Lina: ops-bot posted a node event: rack-12 switch reported intermittent crc errors at 08:19, link 3.
ops-bot: switch/rack-12 port-3 crc-errors incremented (count=42) 1 08:19:12 - auto-escalate to INC-2032.
Diego: paste of interesting lines: 
```
Scheduler: candidate node=node-ap-southeast12 warmpool_protected=true age=24m
LeaseManager: handshake attempts=4 last_err=deadline exceeded
Kubelet: eviction_threshold met memory.available=120Mi
NetworkDriver: tx_drop=12 rx_crc=42 if=eth1
```
Nina: The warmpool age is >20m which normally allows reclaim, but we still obeyed guard because lease handshake failed repeatedly. That blocked packing and increased fragmentation.
Harpreet: Reasonable hypothesis: egress shaping + switch errors caused delayed kubelet heartbeats -> lease handshake failures -> warmpool protection prevented reclaim -> tiny pods in queue.
Kostas: Suggestion: add a scheduler policy that treats repeated net CRCs/tx drops as "unhealthy" and allow emergency reclaim after N failures. Could be a toggle behind a feature flag.
Lina: Ops mitigation we tried: cleared the port error counters and disabled per-port policing for 10m. After that node heartbeats returned and scheduler reclaimed two warmpool slots.
Diego: We should be careful with disabling policing at scale. It removes a line of defense for noisy tenants. Maybe limit to a single rack emergency window and track billing delta.
Harpreet: Implementation plan: 1) track warmpool_protected_age metric per node, 2) if age > 15m AND lease_handshake_failures > 3 AND net_crc_count > 10 -> mark node as "reclaimable-unhealthy" and allow preempt. 3) expose toggle in console.
Nina: + add audit log entry for any emergency reclaim so we can reconcile which pods got force-evicted.
Kostas: I'll draft a small RFC and a POC in the scheduler that flips the guard when net errors are observed. Will include a metric warmpool_emergency_reclaims_total.
Lina: Ops will coordinate a one-off unpolicing window if you need a manual canary for the change, but prefer to test in canary region first.
Diego: Also note cost impact: when we reclaimed slots aggressively previously, we saw slight increase in transient GPU spin-ups due to reassigning pods, cost ~0.6% token-hours for the day. Worth tracking.
Harpreet: Agree - we'll add cost dashboard tile tied to warmpool_emergency_reclaims_total.
Nina: Action items: Lina create INC-2032 and attach switch counters, Kostas write RFC + PR, Harpreet add metric and console toggle, Diego collect cost delta baseline.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout (3 nodes) of scheduler-guard-prototype to ap-southeast1 in 30m.
Kostas: tagging the RFC draft: https://github.com/redwood/scheduler/pull/410 (draft).
Diego: If canary looks good, let's gate global rollout on 7d of stable metrics and <5% increase in eviction churn.
Nina: Thanks all, will follow up after canary. Update here with INC-2032 notes.
